requiredFindings.title: SM-14’s exact subject-count map omits Rspack and Sui
requiredFindings.evidence: otherFigures.SM14.S is formed only from medium census rows and the two analysed large-census workloads. It contains Smithy1084 and Deno1052 but no poly-large-rspack or rs-very-large-sui. The same pinned report data already contains their accepted subject counts1384 and3318 in otherFigures.SM12.rows. The report nevertheless states S is exact per workload and directs readers to otherFigures.SM14.S.
requiredFindings.impact: The purported per-workload SM-14 input map is incomplete for two item9/section3a workloads. Lack of analysed compiler coverage does not make the independent subject counts unavailable.
requiredFindings.requiredCorrection: Populate otherFigures.SM14.S from the complete accepted subject-count records, adding poly-large-rspack=1384 and rs-very-large-sui=3318 with Sui’s existing conditional standing. Cross-check agreement where census counts also exist and assert complete expected workload coverage. Preserve K_stage/stages and other owned parameters as unset; regenerate data/report/manifest. No measurement rerun or stage-budget computation is needed.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Render analysed-entry counts instead of Python object lists
nonBlockingObservations.evidence: The large-workload table’s Analysed entries cells print full entries lists, including private cwd paths and control flags, for Smithy and Deno. These are the correct10 and2 entries but obscure the intended summary.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestion: Render len(entries) in the summary table and keep detailed entry objects in pinned machine data.
